newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Benelux says banks extend agreement.
newsitem.headline: Benelux says banks extend agreement.

text.p: Data storage products maker Benelux International Ltd said on Monday its standstill agreement with its bankers has been extended for another month, to October 31.

Benelux entered into an interim standstill agreement with its banks on June 28 whereby the banks agreed to continue to support the group by not demanding repayment of existing bank facilities before September 30 and to make available interim working capital of up to HK$60 million (US$7.76 million) to the group, it said.
Discussions concerning a proposal put forward by the potential investor had been ongoing and no formal agreement had yet been reached, it said.

The banks have been informed that the due diligence on Benelux conducted by the potential investor has not completed yet. The banks have agreed to extend the validity period of the standstill agreement, it said.
Last month Benelux reported a net loss of HK$497.97 million for the year ended March 31, including exceptional loss of HK$384.55 million, compared with HK$47.79 million yearly profit a year ago.
